description: PostgreSQL 18 date parsing, canonical output, BC and Julian calendars, infinity, arithmetic, ordering, and range validation
sql: CREATE TABLE type_matrix_date (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value DATE UNIQUE);
SELECT id, value FROM type_matrix_date ORDER BY value, id;

SELECT '2024-2-3'::date AS short_iso, '02/03/2024'::date AS mdy, 'February 3, 2024'::date AS named, '2024-034'::date AS ordinal, 'J2451545'::date AS julian, '0001-01-01 BC'::date AS bc, '+infinity'::date AS positive_infinity;

SELECT '2024-02-29'::date + 1 AS date_plus, 1 + '2024-02-29'::date AS plus_date, '2024-03-01'::date - 1 AS date_minus, '2024-03-01'::date - '2024-02-28'::date AS date_difference, '0001-01-01 BC'::date + 1 AS bc_plus, '0001-01-01 BC'::date - 1 AS bc_minus, 'infinity'::date + 1 AS infinity_plus;
SELECT '-infinity'::date < '0001-01-01 BC'::date AS negative_order, '0001-01-01 BC'::date < '0001-01-01'::date AS bc_order, 'infinity'::date > '5874897-12-31'::date AS positive_order;
SELECT id FROM type_matrix_date WHERE value = 'February 3, 2024'::date;
SELECT '4714-11-24 BC'::date AS minimum_date, '5874897-12-31'::date AS maximum_date;
